description.value: JFrog describes itself as 'The Single Source of Truth for the Agentic Software Supply Chain,' a platform that establishes, enforces, and tracks trust in software across DevOps, DevSecOps, DevGovOps, and AI security.
JFrog sells a software supply chain platform for DevOps, security, and AI teams, covering artifact management, security scanning, governance, and AI asset control.
A DevOps and software supply chain company that develops a software supply chain platform to help companies deliver software faster and more reliably.
An Israeli software company, now listed on Nasdaq as FROG.

product_description.value: DevOps: Artifactory, Distribution, and Connect. DevSecOps: Curation, Xray, Zero-Touch Remediation, and Advanced Security. AgentSecOps: AI Security, Agent Guard, and AI asset scanning. DevGovOps: AppTrust.

Artifactory (universal artifact and AI asset management), Xray (software composition analysis), Curation, Advanced Security, Distribution, Connect (IoT device management), AI Security and Agent Guard, AppTrust (continuous governance and compliance), Zero-Touch Remediation, and JFrog Boost and Agent Plugin for coding agents.
Flagship Artifactory, plus Xray (security and compliance scanning), Pipelines (CI/CD), Mission Control, and Distribution; one source also lists Connect.

business_model_description.value: Primarily sells subscriptions, offered as SaaS, with revenue from subscriptions, licenses, professional services, and training. Pricing is tiered, and growth comes largely from upselling customers to more expensive packages.

customer_description.value: Trusted by over 80% of the Fortune 100; logos include Volvo, TripAdvisor, Fidelity, Google, Airbus, American Express, NVIDIA, Red Hat, and SAP.
Trusted by over 80% of the Fortune 100; logos include Volvo, Google, NVIDIA, SAP, and American Express.
Sectors cited include financial, public, technology, healthcare, gaming, and automotive. A 2020-era analysis reported 75% of Fortune 100 and 27% of Forbes Global 2000 companies as customers.
